body:
**Special situations: spin-offs**
- Cusatis, Miles and Woolridge (1993) studied 815 spin-offs from 1965–1988. They found significantly positive abnormal returns for the spun-off company, the parent and the combined pair for up to 3 years, attributed largely to takeovers of these firms. — [Academia.edu, "Restructuring through spinoffs"](https://www.academia.edu/87621500/Restructuring_through_spinoffs)
- McConnell, Ozbilgin and Wahal (2001) found the post-spin-off returns are a "shaky basis" for beating the market. A 2007 EFMA paper says later research shows post-spin-off firms do not earn the same long-run abnormal returns. **The spin-off edge popularized by Greenblatt is contested and may have decayed.** — [Purdue / McConnell 2001](https://business.purdue.edu/faculty/mcconnell/publications/spinoffs-ex-ante-2001-vol74.pdf); [EFMA 2007 paper](https://www.efmaefm.org/0EFMAMEETINGS/EFMA%20ANNUAL%20MEETINGS/2007-Austria/papers/0607.pdf)

**13F / superinvestor tracking**
- Institutions may delay quarter-end 13F disclosure by up to 45 days. The average filer takes about 37 days, and some managers use the delay to hide trades. — [AEA 2017 working paper](https://aeastaging.aeaweb.org/conference/2017/preliminary/paper/aiTbZ9QD); [Christoffersen et al. paper](https://www.bwl.uni-mannheim.de/media/Lehrstuehle/bwl/Area_Finance/Finance_Area_Seminar/HWS2018/Christoffersen_Paper.pdf)
- Academic results as reported secondhand (I did not open the original papers):
  - Verbeek and Wang (2012) found that replicating hedge funds' top holdings produced significant alpha even after the 45-day lag.
  - Agarwal et al. (2013) found that hedge fund buys beat their sells by about 1.5% per quarter.
  - Aragon, Martin and Shi (2019) found that much of the "superstar" alpha is earned **before** the filing is public.
  — [Arkolith blog](https://arkolith.com/blog/copy-trading-hedge-funds); [InvestorLens](https://www.investorlens.capital/docs/faq/can-filings-predict-performance)
- One commercial backtest reports that 63 of 76 super-investors trail SPY when cloned with the realistic lag. Its methodology is unverified. It attributes the gap partly to 13Fs omitting shorts, bonds, foreign listings and cash. Cloning works best for low-turnover managers. — [HoldLens](https://holdlens.pages.dev/learn/copy-trading-myth/); [InvestorLens blog](https://www.investorlens.capital/blog/2026-10-16-13f-45-day-lag-how-to-use-it)

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:GENUSPOWER:cold-valuation-beats-nifty-to-jun27`
- **Method:** valuation-temperature · **P(ours)** 0.52 · **P(base)** 0.45 · resolve by 2027-06-30
- **Evidence:** screener.in 20-Nov-2026: price ₹266, P/E 11.9 vs its own 5-yr median P/E 38.3 (≈0.3× own median — 'cold'); ROCE 25.3%, ROE 30.9%; 52-wk range ₹207–359. Known flags (memdb event:GENUSPOWER:avoid-2026-11-19): CFO negative 3 years (smart-meter AMISP model), borrowings ~₹2,482 cr, FII 18.7%→7.4%. Nifty 50 close 20-Nov-2026: 25,800.6 (Yahoo ^NSEI).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Valuation-temperature test of the cold end: a stock at ~0.3× its own median multiple with high reported ROE. Lesson L12 cuts both ways — cheap can stay cheap when cash conversion is poor, so we are only mildly above base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** A single Indian small cap beats the Nifty 50 over a ~7-month window roughly 45% of the time (return skew: the median small cap lags the index).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if (Genus close on NSE 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 266.0) > (Nifty 50 close 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust Genus for any split/bonus; dividends ignored for both.
- **Resolution source:** NSE/Yahoo Finance closes (GENUSPOWER.NS, ^NSEI); screener.in price
- **Sources used:** https://www.screener.in/company/GENUSPOWER/consolidated/; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5ENSEI

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-CAT:dividend-raise-7pct-by-jun27`
- **Method:** base rate · **P(ours)** 0.72 · **P(base)** 0.75 · resolve by 2027-06-30
- **Evidence:** 8-K 11-Jun-2026: Board raised quarterly dividend by 12 cents (+8%) to $1.63, 'maintains our place on the S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats Index'. Prior June raises (from memory): 2023 +8%, 2024 +8%, 2025 +7%. Q3 2026 8-K: $1.2B buybacks + $0.7B dividends in the quarter; enterprise cash $7.9B; operating cash flow $4.4B.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Pattern is very stable and cash generation strong; the main risk is a smaller raise if the machinery cycle softens (rate hikes globally).
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Persistence: 4 of 4 recent June raises were ≥7%; generic aristocrat repeat-size base ~75%.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if, on or before 30-Jun-2027, Caterpillar declares a regular quarterly dividend ≥ $1.745 per share (rounded: ≥$1.75).
- **Resolution source:** Caterpillar dividend 8-K / press release (SEC EDGAR, CIK 18230)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/18230/000110465926072929/tm2617177d1_8k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/18230/000001823026000052/0000018230-26-000052-index.htm

- **Group revenue, both years.** FY25: cut in Feb-25 to 12-13% standalone / 13-15% consolidated; delivered +12.7% / +13.7%. FY26: guided "20%+" in the May-25 opening remarks; delivered +22.9% standalone (INR 23,210 cr) and +21.6% consolidated (INR 27,143 cr). Also ~98.7% of the "INR 25,000 cr + ~10%" revised Vision target.
- **Margins.** Q4FY25 standalone PBT "~5%" -> 5.9%. FY26 consolidated PBT 4.5-4.75% -> 4.9% before exceptional items (+120 bp; screener 5.05%). "+50 bp minimum" -> +120 bp consolidated.
- **Working capital, debt and finance cost - every target met.** Standalone NWC <100 days: 94 (Mar-25), 90 (Mar-26), 81 (Sep-26). Finance cost "mid-2%" then "<2%": 1.4% (Q4FY25), 1.6% (FY26; screener quarterly sum 368 / 23,211). Net debt ~1x EBITDA "very soon": 1.06x at Mar-25, consolidated net debt INR 915 cr at Mar-26 and INR 72 cr at Sep-26. "Mar-26 net debt much lower than Dec": 915 vs 2,240.
- **Order inflow.** FY26 INR 26,000-28,000 cr guided -> ">26,000" (bottom of range). FY27 >30,000 guided; INR 23,934 cr by 05-Nov-26.
- **Segments:** T&D +25% (vs 20%+), B&F +19% (18-20%), Urban Infra +49% (40-50%), LMG Sweden +64% (30-40%) with EBITDA 6.7-6.8% (vs 5-6.25%).
- **Water collections** of INR 500-700 cr in Q4FY25 (~610 received), and "improve in Q4FY26" (delivered).
